analysis.title: Honeywell International Inc. (HON): Takeaways from our investor meeting
key_insights: GS hosted an investor dinner with HON's SVP of Investor Relations Mark Macaluso. Management sounded constructive on 2027, citing nearly $19bn of backlog, resilient short-cycle demand and ongoing self-help.
Management expects 2027 organic growth toward the higher end of its 4% to 6% long-term framework, with volumes improving after a largely price-driven 2026. GS expects mid-teens+ EPS growth in 2027.

Backlog gives visibility into 2028, particularly for LNG projects, which typically convert over 18 to 24 months. PA&T is expected to be the fastest-growing segment in 2027 as project backlog converts.
Current PA&T growth is driven mainly by Process Technology. The Process Automation cycle has not yet meaningfully started, which is an added growth opportunity over time.
PA&T orders excluding the large project comparison are expected to improve considerably as global mega-projects firm up and catalyst/adsorbents orders keep improving.

Building Automation (BA) is benefiting from fire, security and access control demand. Data centers should be about 5% of BA revenue by YE26 and possibly about 10% over time as BA scales toward $10bn. $7bn of BA's $8bn 2026 sales is short cycle.
GS expects management to guide 2027 conservatively (+MSD organic) with upside as the year progresses. Pricing is expected to stay around 4% at least through 1H27.

Management reiterated confidence in reaching about 22% Industrial Automation (IA) margins in 4Q26 and sees about 23% as achievable in 2027, supported by funded restructuring, productivity and divestiture benefits. The underlying core business is already comfortably above 20% margins.

IA is copying BA's commercial playbook (regional sales leadership, vertical-focused management, improved sales incentives) to support longer-term organic growth. Management expects y/y IA margin improvement throughout 2027 despite a seasonally softer 1Q.
PA&T margins are pressured by unfavorable project mix, inflation and the Johnson Matthey (JM) integration. JM is expected to add about $175mn of revenue at roughly zero segment margin in 4Q26.

PA&T margins could stay near the about 21.5% 4Q26 exit level in 1H27 before improving meaningfully in 2H27. Management cautioned against overly optimistic 2027 margin expectations. Tailwinds include $60mn to $80mn of JM cost reductions in year one, MSD catalyst growth in 2027 after a roughly flat 2026, and easing raw material inflation.

Management still references about 15% EPS growth as a preliminary 2027 baseline, now off a higher 2026 base. Corporate costs should fall from about $575mn in 2026 to about $400mn in 2027, and below-the-line expenses are expected at about $700mn.

Share count is expected to stay broadly flat, with buybacks limited to offsetting dilution because debt reduction is the priority. Free cash flow conversion could approach about 95% over time, above the 90%+ long-term target.
GS rates HON Buy with a 12-month price target of $266, based on 15.0x Q5-Q8 EBITDA. The stock closed at $224.05 on 3 Nov 2026, implying 18.7% upside.

market_movers.rationale: Improving growth visibility and margin expansion opportunities after the portfolio transformation. Backlog of nearly $19bn and mid-teens+ 2027 EPS growth expected.

earnings_insights: GS forecasts HON EPS (estimates) of $8.45 for 12/26E, $9.80 for 12/27E and $11.05 for 12/28E, versus $6.46 for 12/25.
GS quarterly EPS estimates: $2.27 for 9/26 (as shown in the GS forecast table), $2.47 for 12/26E, $2.06 for 3/27E and $2.39 for 6/27E.
Management references about 15% 2027 EPS growth as a preliminary baseline (company guidance framework, not yet formal guidance). GS expects mid-teens+ EPS growth.
GS 12/27E revenue estimate is $20,470.1mn and EBITDA estimate is $5,702.6mn, versus 12/26E revenue of $20,193.4mn and EBITDA of $4,031.1mn.
